medical-reference-document.title: WHO Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Hypertension in Adults

section.title: WHO Pharmacological Guidelines - Treatment Thresholds and First-Line Classes

sections.section: The World Health Organization (WHO) Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Hypertension in Adults strongly recommends initiating pharmacological antihypertensive treatment in individuals with a confirmed diagnosis of hypertension and SBP >= 140 mmHg or DBP >= 90 mmHg. In individuals with existing cardiovascular disease or high baseline cardiovascular risk, pharmacological treatment is recommended at SBP 130-139 mmHg. Recommended first-line pharmacological agent classes comprise: 1. Thiazide or thiazide-like diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, indapamide). 2. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACE inhibitors) or Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). 3. Long-acting dihydropyridine Calcium channel blockers (CCBs, e.g., amlodipine).

section.title: WHO Pharmacological Guidelines - Combination Therapy and Blood Pressure Targets

sections.section: For adults requiring pharmacological antihypertensive therapy, WHO recommends initial combination therapy with two first-line agents of different classes—ideally as a single-pill fixed-dose combination (SPC)—particularly when baseline SBP is >= 20 mmHg above target. Dual therapy combining an ACE-inhibitor/ARB with either a CCB or a thiazide diuretic achieves significantly faster and more sustained blood pressure control. The target blood pressure for all non-pregnant adults with hypertension is SBP < 140 mmHg and DBP < 90 mmHg, and < 130/80 mmHg in high-risk patients with established CVD or diabetes.
